newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Australian firm in $200 mln Vietnam resort project.
newsitem.headline: Australian firm in $200 mln Vietnam resort project.

text.p: Australian firm Leda Holdings and a Vietnamese partner have begun a feasibility study into a $200 million tourist resort project near Vietnam's central city of Danang, a project official said on Monday.
The project involves the construction of three hotels, several villas and apartments and an 18-hole golf course nine km (five miles) south of the city, the official said.
He said Leda Holdings would hold a stake of around 70 percent while the Danang Tourism Service Company would contribute the remainder in land-use rights.
The feasibility study is expected to be submitted to the Ministry of Planning and Investment by the end of June for approval.

Earlier this year, Vietnam withdrew an American developer's licence to build a luxury holiday resort at Danang's China Beach after the firm, BBI Investment Group, failed to make an initial deposit of $2 million.
China Beach was a rest and recreation area for U.S. soldiers during the Vietnam war.
